subject: Model slate handoff — shortlist, context needs, and token runway for ClearPath AI
messages:

Subject: Model slate handoff — shortlist, context needs, and token runway for ClearPath AI

Hi Emily / ClearPath team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As promised, attaching the initial model shortlist and a set of token-runway scenarios so your engineers and product folks can review. High-level asks from our side so the onboarding workstream can start: 

- Confirm target latency SLO (p50/p95) for interactive flows vs. background batch jobs.
- Confirm average and 95th percentile prompt + response lengths for the top three user journeys you expect to ship in the first 90 days.
- Share any regulatory constraints around data residency or private deployment (we noted you flagged EU customers).

What we attached: model_shortlist (three candidates with rough cost/throughput tradeoffs), token_runway CSV (baseline, growth, and burst scenarios), and a preliminary MAP PDF with responsibilities and milestone dates.

Proposed next steps:
1) Emily: can you confirm the 90-day active-user estimate and % of traffic that is low-latency vs. async?
2) Monica: once we have the numbers, we can convert the token runway to Dedicated vs Hosted capacity recommendations and propose a canary rollout plan.
3) Grace/Jordan: I'll coordinate an internal sizing session to validate batch sizes and caching profiles — aim for Wed 9/1 EOD to get a first draft.

Emily, copying Monica/Grace who will drive the implementation plan.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Park <emily@clearpath.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model slate handoff — shortlist, context needs, and token runway for ClearPath AI

Hi Dylan — thanks for the docs. Quick answers below: 

- 90-day active users: 18k monthly active; expect ~6k daily active on peak days.
- Latency split: ~85% are user-facing chat interactions (target p95 < 800ms), 15% are async summarization jobs that can tolerate 5s.
- Typical prompt+response lengths: chat median =~ 140 tokens total (prompt+response), 95th =~ 720 tokens. Async jobs median 2.2k tokens.
- Data residency: most customers are US-based; one large European hospital pilot will require EU region only for that tenant.

One ask: can Redwood provide recommended quantization/precision options for the shortlisted models and call out any expected accuracy delta for our LLM evaluation suite? Rajesh (cc) will also share a short evaluation harness next hour.

Emily
Product Ops, ClearPath AI

Subject: RE: Model slate handoff — shortlist, context needs, and token runway for ClearPath AI

Emily — great, this is exactly the kind of specificity we need. Quick practical notes after a rapid pass on the attached shortlist: 

Model shortlist (recommended initial order):
1) open-13B-q4f16 (LLM-A) — best latency/cost balance for chat at 140–720 token envelopes. Good steady-state throughput, supports int8/4-bit quant profiles with <3% observed accuracy delta on our evals.
2) redwood-70b-rlhf-int8 (LLM-B variant) — higher quality for 95th-percentile long-context chat and async summarization; expect ~2.2x cost vs LLM-A on tokens but better for hallucination-sensitive workflows.
3) long-context-32k (LLM-C) — purpose-built for the 2.2k+ async jobs and EU tenant with long-doc summarization needs; will need Dedicated capacity for predictable multi-tenant isolation.

Sizing notes (based on your 6k DAU peak, 85% chat, median 140 tokens, p95 720):
- Baseline monthly token estimate (conservative): 18k MAU * 150 tokens average * 30 days ~= 81M tokens/month.
- Peak-day throughput: assume 6k DAU, average session ~4 messages => ~24k requests/day. With p95 lengths, provision for bursts at ~180k tokens/hour (burst scenario).
- Latency targets suggest we configure a 2-tier routing policy: Hosted low-latency pool using LLM-A with aggressive batching (max-batch 32, max-latency 40ms) and Dedicated long-context pool for async + EU tenant.

Quantization recommendations: start with 4-bit quant for LLM-A to minimize RPC overhead; run a focused eval set (Rajesh's harness) to validate delta on safety and extraction tasks. Expect small quality loss on extraction but acceptable for chat.

Attachments: I updated the token_runway_scenarios.csv to show three lanes (conservative, expected, aggressive) and included a quick cost delta column per model.

Next steps / asks:
- Emily: can Rajesh share the evaluation harness link and a sample of 50 async jobs so we can run the LLM-C long-context pass?
- Jordan: please draft a canary timeline (two-week canary, 5% traffic on LLM-A -> then 20% if stable).
- Grace: please create an ops playbook stub for cache warming + prefix caching for common prompts.

I'll join the Wed 9/1 internal sizing session.

Thanks,
Monica
Director, Customer Implementation | Redwood Inference
